proposer.mechanism:
Compound the only-untested-polarity lever from run-4 (min_prob=0.0, kept) with a single additional change on the same axis: raise sensitivity from 2.0 to 3.0. All other base parameters preserved exactly (fast_halflife=20 ticks, slow_halflife=120 ticks, min_ticks=30, max_vol_ratio=5.0, SHA-256 deterministic draw on client_order_id, reduce-only pass-through unconditional). The skip-probability curve becomes p = exp(-3.0 * max(0, vol_ratio - 1)) with no floor. Comparison at key vol_ratio values vs base (sensitivity=2.0, min_prob=0.05):
  vol_ratio=1.0 -> p=1.000 (base 1.000) — identical, calm regime
  vol_ratio=1.2 -> p=0.549 (base 0.670) — moderate compression
  vol_ratio=1.5 -> p=0.223 (base 0.368) — meaningful compression
  vol_ratio=2.0 -> p=0.050 (base 0.135) — steepened mid-tail
  vol_ratio=2.5 -> p=0.011 (base 0.050) — past base floor
  vol_ratio=3.0 -> p=0.0025 (base 0.050 floor) — deep tail crushed
  vol_ratio>=4.0 -> p~0 (base 0.050 floor)
The combined change tests the joint hypothesis that base's tail-skipping curve is BOTH too shallow (sensitivity too low) AND has a redundant floor (min_prob too high). Run-4 isolated the floor (PASS, +0.70%). Run-3 isolated the curve shallowness in the WRONG direction (sensitivity 2.0->1.0 lost -30%). The natural opposite-polarity completion of that test, combined with the validated min_prob=0.0, is sensitivity=3.0 + min_prob=0.0.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Two empirically-grounded facts from this experiment so far: (1) Run-3 demonstrated that LESSENING base's tail-skipping aggressiveness (sensitivity 2.0->1.0) lost 30% of P&L — direct empirical evidence that base's tail-skipping curve is at minimum NOT TOO STEEP. The opposite-polarity test (STEEPER) is the untested direction. (2) Run-4 demonstrated that the min_prob=0.05 floor was preserving non-trivial extreme-tail bad fills — removing it gave +0.70%, the first PASS in this experiment. This implies the WORST-tail bad fills are concentrated where p was already small. But run-4's effect was tiny (~$5 / 12 days) because base's existing curve at sensitivity=2.0 already drops p below ~0.13 by vol_ratio=2.0, so the floor-vs-no-floor difference only mattered for vol_ratio>2.5 — a narrow band. The NEXT lever: bring more of the moderate-vol band into the steep-tail regime by raising sensitivity. At sensitivity=3.0, the steep-skip region kicks in by vol_ratio~1.5 instead of vol_ratio~2.5; the addressable population of skipped trades is roughly 5-10x larger than run-4's tail-only set. Base's NOTES.md per-date pattern (loss-reduction on adverse days 20260313-17 is 22.9-54.4% larger than improvement on good days) implies that the moderate-elevated-vol band (vol_ratio 1.3-2.0) is also adverse-fill-heavy — not just the extreme tail. Run-3's falsification proves this band is genuinely high-loss when participated in fully. Combining min_prob=0.0 (run-4 PASS) + sensitivity=3.0 (run-3's mirror image) targets exactly this moderate-and-tail band.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero-slippage and zero-commission fill model confirmed from execution_algos/vol-regime-sizer/results/backtest-results.json (mean_slippage=0.0, max_abs_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0). All edge from realized P&L. Trade-count downside: at sensitivity=3.0 the algorithm skips substantially more orders than base (estimated ~15-25% of orders below p=0.5, versus base's ~10-15%). This is GREATER than run-4's strict-subset behavior but still well within range of base's own ~3% reduction vs simple. As long as the skipped trades have negative expected P&L per trade (run-3 falsification proves this for the moderate band; run-4 PASS proves this for the deep tail), the net effect is positive. Worst-case downside bounding: (a) if the moderate-elevated band actually contains MORE good trades than bad (contradicting run-3), this variant underperforms base — but run-3 already empirically tested this region in the OPPOSITE direction and lost 30%, so the prior weight is on the moderate-elevated band being adverse-fill-net-negative. (b) The deterministic SHA-256 draw means submission set is reproducible — no variance noise across runs. (c) Reduce-only orders unchanged: intraday_flat compliance preserved.
proposer.builds_on: vrs-pc-r4 (single PASS in this experiment so far, +0.70%). Inherits min_prob=0.0 entirely. Single additional change: sensitivity 2.0 -> 3.0. Architecturally identical to run-4 in every other respect.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) sensitivity=2.5 + min_prob=0.0: smaller effect, less informative as a test of the sensitivity axis. 3.0 is the cleaner symmetric mirror of run-3's 1.0. (2) sensitivity=4.0 + min_prob=0.0: too aggressive; vol_ratio=1.2 already gives p=0.30 — would skip large fraction of normal orders. (3) Keep sensitivity=2.0, lower min_prob below 0.0: not meaningful (min_prob is already at the natural lower bound). (4) Increase max_vol_ratio from 5.0 to higher: only affects the deepest tail where p is already ~0 at sensitivity=3.0 — no meaningful change. (5) Change the estimator (e.g., time-based EWM, Parkinson): orthogonal axis; defer until the sensitivity/floor axis is exhausted. (6) Add a second gating condition (e.g., spread): falsified families in runs 1-2. (7) Asymmetric curve (different slopes above/below vol_ratio=1): adds parameters, untestable in single run. (8) Reduce slow_halflife (faster baseline): changes what 'baseline' means, confounds with curve change.

objections.text: Misreading of run-3's falsification. Run-3 reduced sensitivity 2.0->1.0 AND kept min_prob=0.05. The result (-30% vs base) is a JOINT test of (a) shallower curve, (b) PRESERVED floor at 0.05. The Proposer attributes the loss entirely to (a) — but it could equally well be attributed to (b) interacting with (a): at sensitivity=1.0, the curve only dips below the 0.05 floor at vol_ratio>4.0 (vs sensitivity=2.0 hitting floor at vol_ratio~2.5), so the floor's truncation behavior changes meaningfully. Run-3 does NOT cleanly prove 'the moderate-vol band is adverse-fill-net-negative.' It only proves 'sensitivity=1.0+min_prob=0.05 loses 30%.' Without per-vol-bin EDA on a train date, the Proposer's claim that the moderate-elevated band (vol_ratio 1.3-2.0) is adverse-fill-heavy is an inferential leap, not an empirical fact.

Magnitude calibration unjustified. The Proposer chose sensitivity=3.0 as the 'symmetric mirror' of run-3's 1.0 around base's 2.0. But the exp-decay curve is NOT symmetric in its effect on submission probability: going from 2.0 to 1.0 changes p at vol_ratio=2.0 by 0.135->0.368 (+233%); going from 2.0 to 3.0 changes p at vol_ratio=2.0 by 0.135->0.050 (-63%). These are not the same magnitude of intervention. A more cautious intermediate calibration — sensitivity=2.5 — would test the steeper-curve hypothesis with bounded downside. Run-4 PASSed by ~$5; an aggressive sensitivity=3.0 jump could swing well past +0.70% in either direction. If the moderate-band reading is wrong, this run could give back run-4's entire gain and more. The Criticizer's strong preference is sensitivity=2.5 as the first step on this axis.

Trade-count cliff concern. At sensitivity=3.0, vol_ratio>=1.0 gives p<=1.0 with steep dropoff; integrating against a typical fast/slow EWM ratio distribution (centered near 1 with right-tail), the average submission probability across orders will drop noticeably below run-4's. Run-4 had trade_count=127,992 (vs base 127,991 — essentially identical because the floor change only hit the deep tail). This run would likely shed 10-20% of trades (estimated 100-115k). Lower trade_count amplifies variance in realized_pnl; even a 5% absolute P&L change becomes harder to attribute against the variance of 100k+ correlated samples. The Proposer's claim 'skipped trades have negative expected P&L per trade' must hold strongly enough to overcome this variance amplification AND the lost upside from genuine-positive trades that are now skipped. The +0.70% from run-4 was modest; this run's variance band is wider.

Confounded experiment: combining two changes (sensitivity=3.0 AND min_prob=0.0) means the resulting metrics can't cleanly attribute the change to either lever individually. Run-4 cleanly isolated min_prob. A sensitivity-only run (sensitivity=3.0, min_prob=0.05 unchanged from base) would be the cleanest test of the sensitivity axis. The Proposer should consider whether building on run-4 (inheriting min_prob=0.0) vs building on base (preserving min_prob=0.05) is the right choice for this experiment's interpretability.

The Proposer asserts that the moderate-elevated band is 'roughly 5-10x larger than run-4's tail-only set.' This estimate has no empirical grounding from EDA on the train window. The actual fast/slow EWM ratio distribution on MES quote data is unknown without measurement. The 5-10x figure is plausible but unverified.

suggested_alternatives: sensitivity=2.5 + min_prob=0.0: more conservative first step on the sensitivity axis with bounded downside, still pushes in the right direction.
sensitivity=3.0 + min_prob=0.05 (keep base floor): isolates the sensitivity lever cleanly. Compare to base to attribute the sensitivity change without confounding with the floor change.
EDA on a single train date to measure the vol_ratio distribution and per-bin P&L of base's submitted orders before committing to a specific sensitivity calibration.
criticizer.reasoning: The directional hypothesis (steeper curve + no floor) is plausible and reads runs 3+4 in a reasonable way. But the specific calibration (sensitivity=3.0) is more aggressive than warranted given (a) the joint nature of run-3's test, (b) the asymmetric effect of equal sensitivity deltas, (c) the unmeasured vol_ratio distribution, and (d) the trade-count cliff risk that would amplify variance and could give back run-4's entire +0.70% margin. A sensitivity=2.5 intermediate is the structurally cleaner step on the sensitivity axis with bounded downside.

proposer.mechanism:
Pivot to sensitivity=2.5 + min_prob=0.0 (down from sensitivity=3.0). All other base parameters preserved exactly (fast_halflife=20 ticks, slow_halflife=120 ticks, min_ticks=30, max_vol_ratio=5.0, SHA-256 deterministic draw on client_order_id, reduce-only pass-through unconditional). The skip-probability curve becomes p = exp(-2.5 * max(0, vol_ratio - 1)) with no floor. Comparison at key vol_ratio values vs base (sensitivity=2.0, min_prob=0.05) and vs run-4 (sensitivity=2.0, min_prob=0.0):
  vol_ratio=1.0 -> p=1.000 (base 1.000, run-4 1.000) — identical, calm regime
  vol_ratio=1.2 -> p=0.607 (base 0.670, run-4 0.670) — modest 6pp compression
  vol_ratio=1.5 -> p=0.287 (base 0.368, run-4 0.368) — 8pp compression
  vol_ratio=2.0 -> p=0.082 (base 0.135 floored to 0.05? — no, base floor is 0.05 but 0.135 > 0.05 so base submits at 0.135; run-4 also 0.135) — 5pp compression
  vol_ratio=2.5 -> p=0.024 (base floors at 0.05, run-4 0.018) — past base floor; near run-4
  vol_ratio=3.0 -> p=0.0067 (base floors at 0.05, run-4 0.0025) — past base floor
  vol_ratio>=4.0 -> p<0.002 (base floors at 0.05, run-4 ~0) — past base floor
The sensitivity=2.5 calibration delivers ~5-10pp probability compression across the moderate band (vol_ratio 1.2-2.0) — meaningfully different from base but FAR less aggressive than 3.0's 12-20pp compression. This intermediate step bounds the downside risk to roughly 2x run-4's, not 5x or more.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Joint reading of runs 3 and 4 narrowed: (1) Run-3 (sensitivity 2.0->1.0, min_prob unchanged at 0.05) lost -30%. The Criticizer correctly noted this is a joint shallower-curve + preserved-floor test, but the OUTCOME polarity is unambiguous: the direction sensitivity-lower lost money. The MIRROR direction (sensitivity-higher) is the untested polarity, regardless of whether the loss attribution is curve-shallowness, floor-interaction, or both. (2) Run-4 (min_prob 0.05->0.0, sensitivity unchanged at 2.0) gained +0.70%. This isolates the floor change: removing it helped. The minimal interpolation between these two data points is: 'tighter skipping in the tail helps; looser skipping anywhere hurts.' sensitivity=2.5 extends run-4's helpful-direction slightly further into the moderate band without committing to an aggressive 3.0 jump. The chosen calibration sensitivity=2.5 still 'samples' the new behavior — it's not so close to base that the effect is undetectable, but it's bounded.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero slippage and zero commission per execution_algos/vol-regime-sizer/results/backtest-results.json (mean_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0). Edge from realized P&L only. Trade-count impact: at sensitivity=2.5, the curve compression is modest (5-10pp across vol_ratio 1.2-2.0). Expected trade_count is somewhere between run-4's 127,992 and a hypothetical ~115k floor — modest, not cliff-like. Variance amplification concern is meaningfully reduced relative to sensitivity=3.0. Worst-case bounding: (1) The downside if the moderate-band participation is actually positive-EV is ~2x larger than run-4's tiny effect — manageable. (2) The upside if the moderate-band participation is actually negative-EV (consistent with base's NOTES per-date loss-reduction pattern, though weakly) is ~3-5x larger than run-4's effect. (3) Asymmetric expected payoff favors taking this single conservative step on the sensitivity axis, especially since this is the natural follow-on to the only PASS in the experiment so far. (4) Reduce-only path unchanged: intraday_flat compliance preserved. (5) Submission set is no longer a strict subset of base's because the moderate band is now also affected — but it IS a strict subset of run-4's: at every vol_ratio, p_run5 = exp(-2.5*excess) < exp(-2.0*excess) = p_run4 (for excess > 0). So the test is cleanly attributable to the sensitivity-bump-over-run-4.
proposer.builds_on: vrs-pc-r4 (PASS, +0.70%). Single change vs run-4: sensitivity 2.0 -> 2.5. All other parameters identical to run-4 (including min_prob=0.0 inherited from run-4).
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) sensitivity=3.0 + min_prob=0.0 (round-1 hypothesis): rejected after the Criticizer's three MAJOR objections on misreading run-3, asymmetric exp-decay magnitude, and trade-count cliff variance amplification. (2) sensitivity=3.0 + min_prob=0.05 (Criticizer suggested isolation): plausible as a sensitivity-axis isolation test, but discards run-4's empirically validated min_prob=0.0 — would be a STEP BACK on the lever that we know helps. Prefer to build on the working lever and step forward cautiously on the new one. (3) EDA before committing (Criticizer suggested): EDA on a single train date would measure the vol_ratio empirical distribution and per-bin base submission outcomes, but the bounded-downside design at sensitivity=2.5 makes the empirical test itself a cheap data point — the run IS the EDA at the system level. (4) sensitivity=2.25 (even more conservative): would compress the moderate-band probability by only 3-5pp; the effect would likely be too small to detect against the 12-day variance band, similar to run-4's $5 effect. (5) sensitivity=2.5 + min_prob=0.02 (intermediate floor): two-variable change confounds attribution. (6) Larger fast_halflife or slow_halflife: changes the SENSOR, orthogonal axis; defer.
proposer.revision_notes: Round-1's sensitivity=3.0 hypothesis was abandoned in full after the Criticizer raised three concurrent MAJOR objections: (a) the run-3 falsification is not a clean attribution to the curve shallowness alone — it could equally implicate the floor preservation; (b) the exp-decay curve is asymmetric in probability-space around base's sensitivity=2.0, so a 'symmetric mirror' framing is flawed; (c) the trade-count cliff at sensitivity=3.0 amplifies variance enough to risk giving back run-4's entire +0.70% gain. The Criticizer's preferred alternative (sensitivity=2.5) is structurally the right intermediate step — it preserves the directional bet (steeper curve) but bounds the magnitude to roughly 2x run-4's effect rather than 5x. The MINOR objection about confounding with min_prob is acknowledged but unchanged in the pivot: building on run-4 inherits min_prob=0.0, which makes this run a clean test of (sensitivity-only-over-run-4); the comparison to base mixes both levers, but the comparison to run-4 is single-lever. The MINOR objection about unmeasured vol_ratio distribution is acknowledged — the run itself acts as the measurement at this conservative calibration. Pivot retains the inheritance from run-4 (the only PASS) rather than reverting to base, which the Criticizer's alternative-2 suggested but which would lose the validated lever.

objections.text: The strict-subset claim relative to run-4 is correct (p_run5 < p_run4 for all vol_ratio>1.0 with both at min_prob=0.0). This makes the run-4-vs-run-5 comparison clean. However, the loop.json's vs_base_pnl_pct metric compares to base (vol-regime-sizer), not to run-4 — so the reported headline number will mix the sensitivity lever (run-5-vs-run-4) AND the floor lever (run-4-vs-base, already validated). Implementation must include vs-run-4 attribution in NOTES.md backtest observations to avoid confounded interpretation.

The expected effect magnitude '3-5x run-4's' assumes the moderate-vol band trades are similarly adverse-EV as the deep-tail trades — which is exactly what's untested. If the per-trade adverse-EV magnitude scales roughly inversely with vol_ratio (worst trades concentrated at highest vol_ratio), the actual effect could be smaller than 3-5x even though the affected population is larger. This is acceptable for a bounded-downside experiment, but the Proposer should set expectations: this run is exploratory of the moderate band, not a high-confidence amplifier.

Implementation must preserve all cold-start branches verbatim from run-4 (which itself preserved them from base). The only diff vs run-4 is the sensitivity constant 2.0 -> 2.5 in __init__ and in the factory function default. No accidental refactoring of _compute_submit_prob, on_quote_tick, _order_uniform, or on_order branches.

criticizer.reasoning: The pivot to sensitivity=2.5 + min_prob=0.0 cleanly addresses all three round-1 MAJOR objections: the directional bet is preserved while the magnitude is bounded to ~2x run-4's effect, the trade-count cliff risk is mitigated, and the inferential leap is acknowledged rather than asserted. The strict-subset property relative to run-4 makes the comparison to the only-PASS in this experiment a clean single-lever attribution of the sensitivity axis. No clearly superior untried alternative remains within the scope of building on run-4's validated lever — sensitivity=3.0+min_prob=0.05 would step back from a validated change, EDA is informative but not necessary at this conservative calibration, and sensitivity=2.25 would likely be undetectable. Remaining concerns are MINOR (attribution clarity, magnitude uncertainty, implementation discipline).
